tasks.short: Supervise technicians, analysts, and other engineers.

steps.what: Supervise technicians, analysts, and other engineers
Sign the shift note in the engineer's own words

tasks.design: Supervision stays on the floor. The engineer signs a shift note in {DOCS} in their own words, and a job files that version. No score of a named person is produced, and no decision about a person is made by a job.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shift notes were informal, so later readers could not see what had been decided.
tasks.enabler_now: A note can be filed in the existing document store.
tasks.still_hard: Judging the day's work still requires being there.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer decides what to say about the shift and about the people on it.
tasks.altitude: The week of supervision does not shrink. Only filing the signed note moves.

reach.task: Follow up the signed shift note
reach.learn: That the note is not a score

evidence.claim: Digest [S18] bars a solely automated decision about a worker, so a decision about a person stays with the engineer.
The engineering digest says advice, design, and research stay manual, and the signing engineer stays responsible.

assumptions: The note is the engineer's words, not a generated score.
Configure the document store before a new tool.
unknowns: Whether shift notes are kept in the personnel file.
research_questions: Whether a works council expects to see the note template before it is used.

already_counted.description: Supervising the shift stays inside the remaining time of that step.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only row collection and filing move to a job. Inspection, the decision, and the signature stay with the engineer, after a small upkeep allowance.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design, install, or troubleshoot manufacturing equipment.

steps.what: Troubleshoot manufacturing equipment on the shop floor
Install or adjust the equipment with a technician

outputs: filed copy of signed equipment release v1

tasks.design: Design, install, and troubleshooting stay on the equipment. The engineer signs a release note in {DOCS}, and a job files that version. A model does not change a safety function. The technician's time on the install is not counted as the engineer's.
tasks.previous_blocker: Release notes were written after the fact, and the safety setting lived only on the machine.
tasks.enabler_now: A signed note can be filed in the existing store once the engineer has finished on the floor.
tasks.still_hard: The fault and the install still have to be done in person.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer decides when the equipment is fit to run, including any safety function.
tasks.altitude: Floor time does not shrink. Filing the signed release is the part that moves.

reach.task: Complete the install the note describes

evidence.claim: Digest [S14] says the Machinery Regulation covers AI safety functions from 20 January 2027, so this design does not let a model change a machine safety function.
The engineering digest says advice, design, and research stay manual, and the signing engineer stays responsible.

assumptions: No job writes to the machine.
The note records what the engineer already did.
unknowns: Which safety functions a change can touch.
Who else must sign a release.
research_questions: Whether the firm treats this equipment as in scope of machinery rules.

already_counted.description: Floor troubleshooting stays inside the remaining time of that step.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only row collection and filing move to a job. Inspection, the decision, and the signature stay with the engineer, after a small upkeep allowance.

tasks.short: Evaluate manufactured products against specifications and quality standards.

steps.what: Evaluate manufactured products against the specification
Compare gauge readings with quality standards
Decide if the product meets the quality standard

outputs: filed copy of signed product evaluation v1

tasks.design: The engineer evaluates the product in person. A job compares gauge readings already taken with the quality standards in {SPREADSHEET}. The engineer decides, signs the evaluation in {DOCS}, and a job files that version. A match to the table is not the decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings and the look of the product were judged in one untraced step.
tasks.enabler_now: Standards and readings are already in tables.
tasks.still_hard: A product can meet the numbers and still look wrong.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer decides whether the product meets the standard.

ambition.what: Flag a reading outside the standard before the engineer sees the batch.

tasks.altitude: The engineer still sees the product. Comparing the readings shrinks.

reach.task: Quarantine a batch the signed evaluation rejects

evidence.claim: The engineering digest says root-cause work can use a dashboard and statistics on recorded measurements, with the engineer still deciding the cause.
Digest [S20] records that a paper was withdrawn because the institution had no confidence in its data, so a figure enters a note only when it traces to a source row.

assumptions: The job does not invent a reading.
Configure the standards table before a new store.
unknowns: Who may override a failed reading.
Which standards apply to this product.
research_questions: How often the gauge and the specification use different units.

already_counted.description: Evaluating the product stays inside the remaining time of that step.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

tasks.short: Estimate costs, production times, and staffing for new designs.

steps.what: Estimate costs and production times for new designs
Multiply bill quantities by the price table
Read supplier quotes and check them against totals

loop.purpose: Read quote lines and compare them with the cost total
loop.input: supplier quote and the priced lines
loop.check: the quote total equals the sum of its lines
loop.stop: stop when a line has no price or the totals differ
loop.why_not_simpler: quote layouts differ, so one fixed cell map misses lines

steps.what: Accept staffing requirements for the new design
Sign the cost and staffing estimate

outputs: filed copy of signed cost estimate v1

tasks.design: The engineer sets quantities and staffing for the new design. A job in {SPREADSHEET} multiplies quantities by the price table. A bounded read checks supplier quotes in {EMAIL} against those totals. The engineer signs the estimate in {DOCS}, and a job files that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Estimates were retyped, and a quote total could hide a line that did not match.
tasks.enabler_now: The bill and the price table can be multiplied by a fixed rule.
tasks.still_hard: Staffing still depends on how the line actually runs.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer accepts the cost and the staffing requirement.

ambition.what: Reprice a design when the price table changes, before the estimate is signed again.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends the estimate on quantities and staffing, not on arithmetic.

reach.learn: Which price table version was used

evidence.claim: The engineering digest says a cost estimate is quantities times a price table, and a model may only read supplier quotes that are checked against totals.
Digest [S20] records that a paper was withdrawn because the institution had no confidence in its data, so a figure enters a note only when it traces to a source row.

assumptions: A quote that does not match its lines is not used.
The price table is the price source.
unknowns: Whether staffing ratios are standard or local.
research_questions: How often quotes arrive as pictures the read cannot parse.

already_counted.description: Setting quantities and staffing stays inside the remaining time of those steps.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

role.altitude: The manufacturing engineer spends the week on cause, design, and the signed decision. Collecting rows and filing a signed note move to a job.
reach: Quality technicians get a field list for the part they collect, instead of a blank request.
Planners wait for the signed note before they move a routing.
skills_to_grow: Reject a figure that has no source row.
Release only the version they signed, and leave a safety function to a person.
role.ambitious_version: A signed change note can open a controlled routing update, and the engineer still releases it.
